title: 第二層思考要考慮的事
en: What Second-Level Thinkers Take into Account

vocab.example: Second-level thinking is deep, complex and convoluted.
vocab.def: 原指捲曲、盤繞，比喻事情有很多層次、很難理清。與 deep、complex 並列，強調第二層思考很不簡單。
vocab.exzh: 第二層思考是深入、複雜而且錯綜曲折的。

vocab.example: The second-level thinker takes a great many things into account
vocab.def: 把某些因素一併考慮進去。受詞可以放在中間：take a great many things into account。
vocab.exzh: 第二層思考者會把非常多的事情納入考量

vocab.example: How does the current price for the asset comport with the consensus view of the future, and with mine?
vocab.def: 正式用語，指兩者吻合。這裡是問：現在的價格，和市場共識、和我自己的看法，各自吻合到什麼程度。
vocab.exzh: 這項資產目前的價格，和市場對未來的共識看法吻合到什麼程度？和我的看法又吻合到什麼程度？

vocab.def: 大多數人一致的看法。在投資裡，市場共識反映在價格上，第二層思考者要找出自己和共識的差異。

vocab.example: Is the consensus psychology that’s incorporated in the price too bullish or bearish?
vocab.def: bull（牛）往上頂，代表看漲；bear（熊）往下拍，代表看跌。分別為「看多的」、「看空的」。
vocab.exzh: 已經反映在價格裡的市場共識心理，是過於看多還是過於看空？

vocab.meaning: 正好相反的事物、對立面
vocab.example: Second-level thinkers know that success in investing is the antithesis of simple.
vocab.def: 不只是「不同」，而是完全相反。the antithesis of simple 就是「與簡單正好相反」。
vocab.exzh: 第二層思考者知道，投資成功與簡單正好相反。

vocab.example: That’s not to say you won’t run into plenty of people who try their darnedest to make it sound simple.
vocab.def: 偶然碰到人或事。you won’t run into plenty of people 是「你會碰到很多這樣的人」。
vocab.exzh: 這並不是說你不會碰到很多人，他們拚命想把它說得很簡單。

vocab.example: That’s not to say you won’t run into plenty of people who try their darnedest to make it sound simple.
vocab.def: darnedest 是 damnedest 的委婉說法，比 try one’s best 更口語、更用力。
vocab.exzh: 這並不是說你不會碰到很多人，他們拚命想把它說得很簡單。

vocab.example: Some of them I might characterize as “mercenaries.”
vocab.def: 原指為錢打仗的傭兵，這裡指只在乎賺錢、不真心為你著想的人，如券商與基金公司。
vocab.exzh: 我可能會把其中一些人稱為「唯利是圖者」。

vocab.example: Others who simplify are what I think of as “proselytizers.”
vocab.def: proselytize 是熱心地勸人接受某種信仰或主張。這裡指真心相信、並熱情鼓吹「投資很簡單」的人。
vocab.exzh: 其他把投資簡化的人，是我所認為的「傳教士」。

vocab.example: Others are well-intentioned practitioners who overestimate the extent to which they’re in control
vocab.def: 與 academic（學者）相對，指實際做這行的人。well-intentioned 是「出於善意的」。
vocab.exzh: 另一些人是出於善意的實務工作者，他們高估了自己能掌控的程度

vocab.example: I think most of them fail to tote up their records
vocab.def: 把數字加起來。tote up their records 就是把自己的成績單認真算一次，看看到底賺多少、賠多少。
vocab.exzh: 我認為他們大多數人沒有把自己的成績算清楚

vocab.example: I think most of them fail to tote up their records, or they overlook their bad years or attribute losses to bad luck.
vocab.def: 沒看見或故意不看。overlook their bad years 是「對自己的壞年頭視而不見」。
vocab.exzh: 我認為他們大多數人沒有把自己的成績算清楚，或是忽略自己表現不好的年份，或把虧損歸咎於運氣不好。

vocab.def: attribute A to B 是「把 A 歸因於 B」。注意作為動詞時重音在第二音節；名詞「屬性」則重音在第一音節。
vocab.exzh: 把虧損歸咎於運氣不好

vocab.example: All investors can’t beat the market since, collectively, they are the market.
vocab.def: 把所有人合起來看。作者用這個字說明：全體投資人加起來，就是市場本身。
vocab.exzh: 所有投資人不可能都勝過市場，因為整體而言，他們就是市場。

sentences.en: Second-level thinking is deep, complex and convoluted.
sentences.zh: 第二層思考是深入、複雜而且錯綜曲折的。

sentences.en: The second-level thinker takes a great many things into account:
sentences.zh: 第二層思考者會把非常多的事情納入考量：

sentences.en: What is the range of likely future outcomes?
sentences.zh: 未來可能出現的結果範圍有多大？

sentences.en: Which outcome do I think will occur?
sentences.zh: 我認為會出現哪一種結果？

sentences.en: What’s the probability I’m right?
sentences.zh: 我是對的機率有多高？

sentences.en: What does the consensus think?
sentences.zh: 市場共識是怎麼想的？

sentences.en: How does my expectation differ from the consensus?
sentences.zh: 我的預期和市場共識有什麼不同？

sentences.en: How does the current price for the asset comport with the consensus view of the future, and with mine?
sentences.zh: 這項資產目前的價格，和市場對未來的共識看法吻合到什麼程度？和我的看法又吻合到什麼程度？

sentences.en: Is the consensus psychology that’s incorporated in the price too bullish or bearish?
sentences.zh: 已經反映在價格裡的市場共識心理，是過於看多還是過於看空？

sentences.en: What will happen to the asset’s price if the consensus turns out to be right, and what if I’m right?
sentences.zh: 如果市場共識是對的，資產價格會怎麼變？如果是我對了，又會怎麼變？

sentences.en: The difference in workload between first-level and second-level thinking is clearly massive, and the number of people capable of the latter is tiny compared to the number capable of the former.
sentences.zh: 第一層與第二層思考所需要的工作量，差距顯然極大，而有能力做到後者的人，比起能做到前者的人，數量少得可憐。

sentences.en: First-level thinkers look for simple formulas and easy answers.
sentences.zh: 第一層思考者尋找簡單的公式和容易的答案。

sentences.en: Second-level thinkers know that success in investing is the antithesis of simple.
sentences.zh: 第二層思考者知道，投資成功與簡單正好相反。

sentences.en: That’s not to say you won’t run into plenty of people who try their darnedest to make it sound simple.
sentences.zh: 這並不是說你不會碰到很多人，他們拚命想把它說得很簡單。

sentences.en: Some of them I might characterize as “mercenaries.”
sentences.zh: 我可能會把其中一些人稱為「唯利是圖者」。

sentences.en: Brokerage firms want you to think everyone’s capable of investing—at $10 per trade.
sentences.zh: 券商希望你以為每個人都有能力投資——一筆交易只要 10 美元。

sentences.en: Mutual fund companies don’t want you to think you can do it;
sentences.zh: 共同基金公司不希望你以為自己做得到；

sentences.en: they want you to think they can do it.
sentences.zh: 他們要你以為他們做得到。

sentences.en: In that case, you’ll put your money into actively managed funds and pay the associated high fees.
sentences.zh: 那樣一來，你就會把錢投入主動式管理基金，並且付出相關的高額費用。

sentences.en: Others who simplify are what I think of as “proselytizers.”
sentences.zh: 其他把投資簡化的人，是我所認為的「傳教士」。

sentences.en: Some are academics who teach investing.
sentences.zh: 有些是教投資的學者。

sentences.en: Others are well-intentioned practitioners who overestimate the extent to which they’re in control;
sentences.zh: 另一些人是出於善意的實務工作者，他們高估了自己能掌控的程度；

sentences.en: I think most of them fail to tote up their records, or they overlook their bad years or attribute losses to bad luck.
sentences.zh: 我認為他們大多數人沒有把自己的成績算清楚，或是忽略自己表現不好的年份，或把虧損歸咎於運氣不好。

sentences.en: Finally, there are those who simply fail to understand the complexity of the subject.
sentences.zh: 最後，還有一些人，單純是不了解這個主題的複雜性。

sentences.en: A guest commentator on my drive-time radio station says, “If you have had good experience with a product, buy the stock.”
sentences.zh: 我在開車時聽的廣播電台，有位特約評論員說：「如果你用過某項產品，經驗不錯，就買它的股票。」

sentences.en: There’s so much more than that to being a successful investor.
sentences.zh: 要成為成功的投資人，要懂的事情遠遠不只這些。

sentences.en: First-level thinkers think the same way other first-level thinkers do about the same things, and they generally reach the same conclusions.
sentences.zh: 第一層思考者對同樣的事，用和其他第一層思考者相同的方式思考，而且通常得到相同的結論。

sentences.en: By definition, this can’t be the route to superior results.
sentences.zh: 依定義，這不可能是通往卓越成果的路。

sentences.en: All investors can’t beat the market since, collectively, they are the market.
sentences.zh: 所有投資人不可能都勝過市場，因為整體而言，他們就是市場。

grammar.point: the former / the latter：前者與後者
grammar.quote: The difference in workload between first-level and second-level thinking is clearly massive, and the number of people capable of the latter is tiny compared to the number capable of the former.
grammar.explain:
the latter 指兩項中的後一項（second-level），the former 指前一項（first-level）。這兩個詞只用在「兩項」的對比，指回前面剛提過的東西。
capable of the latter 是形容詞片語，放在名詞 people／number 後面修飾它；compared to 是分詞片語，「與…相比」。整句是 the number A is tiny compared to the number B。

grammar.point: want you to think …：want ＋ 受詞 ＋ to 動詞，並列對比
grammar.quote: Mutual fund companies don’t want you to think you can do it; they want you to think they can do it.
grammar.explain:
want ＋ 人 ＋ to ＋ 動詞，是「希望某人去…」。後面 think 接了一個沒有 that 的名詞子句：you can do it、they can do it。
兩半句結構完全一樣，只換了主詞，形成「你做得到／他們做得到」的對比，是 Marks 常用的平行句型。

grammar.point: the same way … do：代動詞與關係副詞省略
grammar.quote: First-level thinkers think the same way other first-level thinkers do about the same things, and they generally reach the same conclusions.
grammar.explain:
the same way other first-level thinkers do 是「和其他第一層思考者一樣的方式」，do 代替前面的 think，避免重複。完整是 think the same way (that) other thinkers think。
about the same things 放在 do 之後，修飾整個 think … 動作。把這個句子拆開讀：A think the same way B do / about the same things。
